subject: Healthfolio — PII storage & retention checklist for inference
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Healthfolio — PII storage & retention checklist for inference

Hi Liam / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the items we agreed to validate so you can take this into your privacy review team: 

1) What Redwood stores by default (hosted API):
- Request metadata (timestamps, model id, route) — retained for 30 days for debugging/throughput analytics.
- Optional request/response capture (prompt + output) is OFF by default for new enterprise tenants; when enabled it is retained per tenant TTL.
- Aggregated telemetry (latency, token counts) is retained for 180 days.

2) Options we discussed you might want:
- "No-persist" mode (recommended for PHI-sensitive flows): prompts and outputs are never written to persistent storage; only in-memory for the duration of the API call.
- Sandbox enablement: we can flip a sandbox environment with no-persist enabled to validate functionally.

3) Retention defaults and enterprise options:
- Request logs (metadata only): default 30 days; configurable 0–365 days.
- Audit logs (who called what): default 90 days; enterprise option to export to your S3 for long-term retention (up to 13 months) or to push to your logging endpoint.
- KV-cache / prefix cache: not persisted to durable storage in no-persist mode; otherwise stored in regional cache with TTL you configure.

4) Residency and encryption: 
- We can pin storage and logs to region (us-west-2 or eu-central-1) in Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted can be scoped to region for customer data with enterprise contract.
- Customer-managed keys (KMS) supported for Persistent storage and audit log encryption.

Attachments: I attached a proposed data map (redwood-data-map.xlsx) and a short SOC 2 evidence summary (SOC2-summary.pdf) for your security team to review.

As agreed, could you confirm the following by EOD Tuesday so we can produce the configuration checklist and sandbox: 
- Required residency for Healthfolio patient data (us or eu for EU patients)
- Required retention window for audit logs (months)
- Whether you require outputs (model-generated text) to be never stored in any environment

Next steps from our side once we get your answers: 1) Provision sandbox with no-persist mode; 2) Provide config snippets and an exportable audit-log pipeline; 3) Share a short mutual action plan + DocuSign for the addendum.

Thanks —
Karthik

Thanks Karthik — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing with privacy: 

- Residency: EU patient data must remain in eu-central-1. US patient data can live in us-west-2. So we need region-selection per customer/tenant.
- Outputs: Our default requirement is that model outputs that contain PII should not be persisted. If the output does not contain PII we are OK with short-term capture for debugging (configurable TTL).
- Audit logs: We need audit logs (user + action, timestamp) retained for 12 months. We are happy to accept logs exported to our S3 bucket if Redwood can push them daily.
- Encryption: KMS-managed encryption is required (we prefer customer-managed KMS).

Action items for Redwood: please show exactly how "no-persist" mode prevents outputs from being written (config and operational controls), and include an example export to S3 for audit logs and the names of the S3 objects we should expect.

Priya will coordinate with legal on the addendum — we will return a redline on the data map by EOD Wednesday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Liam

Hi Liam/Priya — quick technical note to make the sandbox demo frictionless and to answer the "exactly how" question:

1) No-persist mode (how it works) - config: 
  - tenant.config.capture_mode = "none"
  - tenant.config.kv_persist = false
  - audit.export.enabled = true (audit metadata only)

2) In-memory only: request payloads and model outputs are kept in memory for the duration of the RPC call; we explicitly avoid serializing / flushing these to disk in our runtime. The tracing hooks that would normally write request/response pairs are gated behind capture_mode and disabled when capture_mode=="none".

3) Audit log export example: 
  - Format: JSON lines with fields {timestamp, tenant_id, user_id, route, action} - Delivery: daily push to your S3 path: s3://healthfolio-redwood-exports/audit/YYYY/MM/DD/*.jsonl - We include a manifest file per day and a signed checksum.

4) KMS: we support attaching your KMS key to the tenant for both persistent artifacts (if any) and the S3 export encryption.

Attached are the config snippets we will push to the sandbox (config-snippets.txt). I can run through a 30-minute tech check once you accept the sandbox invite.

Thanks —
